Hi Lara — thanks, and great next steps. Putting this in writing below and attaching a brief draft PO for reference (ACME_PO_Draft.pdf).

Summary of seller recommendations:
- Term options: we can support 12-month pilot (recommended) or a 24-month discounted term. For pilots we typically price conservatively to make procurement signoff fast; 12mo = list * 0.82 (example), 24mo = list * 0.78.
- Buyer approvals: minimal activation path we recommend:
  1) Procurement approval (Lara) — internal PO creation
  2) Budget owner (dept lead) signoff — optional for pilots under $150k
  3) CFO approval (Tom) — required for >=$150k or multi-year commitments
- Activation SLA: once signed on the private offer, AWS activation typically takes 24–72 hours if the private offer is configured correctly; ask for 7-day activation window in the PO to allow for AWS-side processing and invoice ingestion.

Questions for your team:
- Do you expect finance to want net-30 invoices or net-60?
- Any constraints around purchase order line items or PO references for AWS activation?

Karthik — can you confirm the recommended discount bands and whether a 20% off commitment is feasible for the pilot quantities Lara referenced?

Thanks — attaching ACME_PO_Draft.pdf with example pricing line items.

Quick internal runbook and recommended configuration for ACME private offer:

1) Approval ladder (seller-side mapping):
   - Procurement (buyer) submits PO and approves basic terms — no AWS action needed yet
   - Seller (Redwood) configures private offer and submits to AWS Marketplace with buyer account ID
   - AWS Marketplace processes private offer; activation occurs once buyer accepts the offer in AWS Console
   - Finance (buyer) is invoiced according to the seller-selected invoice flow (seller invoice vs AWS invoice).

2) Term & pricing tradeoffs:
   - 12-month pilot (recommended): faster buyer signoff, smaller upfront commitment, discount ~18–22% depending on volume.
   - 24-month: deeper discount (22–28%) but higher procurement friction for pilots.

3) Activation details & recommendations:
   - Ask buyer to accept within a 7–14 day activation window. If buyer needs a longer activation window, set a 30-day window but document expected start date on the SOW.
   - For finance: if Acme requires seller invoicing (Redwood invoices Acme), we need to enable seller-managed billing. Note: seller-managed billing may require additional tax docs and an early finance handshake; expect 3–5 business days to set up.

4) Risk weighting & approval escalation:
   - If deal value is under $150k ARR equivalent, allow procurement + budget owner.
   - If >$150k or multi-year, escalate to CFO for signature.

Action items:
- Dylan: confirm buyer invoice preference (net-30 vs net-60).
- Dylan/Marissa: include the activation window (proposed 7 days) on the PO and SOW.
- Karthik: confirm exact discount range to pass back to customer by Monday.
